generatedBy: model (not the scorer) — per atlas-fingerprint-DECISION.md, 'The human artifact: 20 minutes, once, blocking'
about: Five ordinal ladders, one per surviving axis. Each ladder is five corpus films ordered
low -> high on that axis ALONE. Rank 1 and rank 5 are the anchors fixed by
docs/specs/atlas-fingerprint-layer.md §3 and re-affirmed by the DECISION; they are shown
to the scorer. Ranks 2-4 are proposed here and are WITHHELD from the scoring prompt, so
reproducing their order is a real test rather than a recital.
The owner audits an argument, not a list: every rung carries one sentence saying why it
sits where it does. Disagree with a sentence and the rung moves.

contract.test: ordinal only. For each axis the scorer's five scores must strictly increase across rank 1..5. Report per-axis, never pooled.
contract.shownToScorer: ranks 1 and 5 only, as the axis anchors, with anchorScore 10 and 90
contract.noNumbersForMiddles: Ranks 2-4 deliberately carry NO target score. Ordinal constraints carry most of the information in an absolute score and are far harder to get wrong. Do not add numbers here.
contract.sampleRequirement: All 15 withheld films (and, for reference, the 10 anchor slots) must be present in the stratified scoring sample, or GATE 3 cannot run at all. Check this before scoring, not after.
contract.breakTest: Shuffle any one ladder's ranks 2-4 in this file and re-run: that axis must report non-compliant while the other four still pass. A gate that stays green on a shuffled ladder is measuring nothing.

constraintsAppliedWhenChoosing: Every film verified present in atlas/static/corpus.json by key; filmId copied from the corpus, not invented.

No withheld rung shares a director with either anchor of its own axis or with another rung of the same axis. A ladder the scorer could satisfy from the crew graph would test the thing this layer exists to escape.
No film appears on two ladders. The only repeats are the anchors the spec itself doubles up: Tokyo Story (cruelty low, fracture low) and Mulholland Drive (ambiguity high, fracture high).
Middles chosen to be separated by a stated argument, not by degree of fame. A ladder whose middle is arguable is a gate that fails for the wrong reason.

knownLimitation.canonicalBias: All 25 ladder films are canonical, which is unavoidable — a ladder film has to be one whose position can be argued. The DECISION's held-out-films note applies directly: anchors' Wikipedia articles run a median 28,026 chars against 5,834 for the long tail. GATE 3 passing therefore says the scorer orders WELL-DOCUMENTED films correctly and says nothing about the 1,324 films carrying no reading. It is not a substitute for reporting MAE per fame stratum.
knownLimitation.anchorsAreNotCeilings: Rank 5 is an anchor, not the corpus maximum. Two corpus films plausibly exceed their axis's high anchor (see poleCaveat on cruelty and fracture). Scores above 90 must remain legal, and GATE 2 pole prevalence must count films past a pole threshold, never films past the anchor.

dread.measures: How much of the running time is spent expecting harm.
dread.doesNotMeasure: Gore, body count, or horror-genre membership. A film can be violent and carry no dread, and carry total dread with nothing happening.

rungs.title: Chungking Express
rungs.why: Nothing in it threatens anyone; even its heartbreak is buoyant, and the film's forward motion is appetite rather than fear.

rungs.title: Rear Window
rungs.why: Its dread is real but rationed — it arrives late, stays inside one courtyard, and is fully discharged by a resolution that hands the film back to the joke.

rungs.title: Picnic at Hanging Rock
rungs.why: Above Rear Window because the dread is never discharged: it is ambient from the first frame, attaches to no villain, and the film ends without explaining or punishing anything.

rungs.title: Rosemary's Baby
rungs.why: Above Picnic because the dread escalates continuously across the whole runtime and is finally confirmed rather than left open, while staying domestic and mannered where Hereditary turns physical.

rungs.title: Hereditary
rungs.director: Ari Aster (corpus records the raw QID Q54864392)
rungs.why: Anchor. Dread is total, continuous and bodily, and the film gives no interval in which it lifts.

weakestAdjacency.risk: A scorer weighting peak intensity over duration could put Picnic above Rosemary's Baby, since unrelieved-and-diffuse can read as worse than escalating-and-confirmed.
weakestAdjacency.ifItFailsHere: Treat as a definitional miss, not a scoring failure, and tighten 'measures' before moving the rung.

alternates.title: Don't Look Now
alternates.note: Swap in if Rosemary's Baby reads too close to Hereditary.

alternates.title: The Shining
alternates.note: Rejected as first choice: arguably level with Hereditary rather than below it, which would make rank 4 vs 5 the coin-flip.

cruelty.measures: How the film treats the people in it — whether harm is deliberate, dwelt on, and shared by the film's own gaze.
cruelty.doesNotMeasure: Sadness. Grave of the Fireflies is devastating and not especially cruel; the axis asks who is doing the hurting and whether the camera stays to watch.

rungs.title: Tokyo Story
rungs.why: Its subject is neglect, and it declines even to punish the neglectful — the harm is real and the film's disposition toward everyone in it is forgiveness.

rungs.title: Bicycle Thieves
rungs.why: The harm is structural and mostly indifferent; the one deliberate cruelty — a crowd humiliating Antonio in front of his son — is brief, and the film's sympathy never withdraws from anyone, including the thief.

rungs.title: Au Hasard Balthazar
rungs.why: Above Bicycle Thieves because cruelty stops being circumstance and becomes intent: named people injure the defenceless, repeatedly and by choice, though Bresson frames it as a passion rather than a spectacle.

rungs.title: Funny Games U.S.
rungs.why: Above Balthazar because cruelty is not a subject but the entire organising principle, extended to the viewer by design — and below Come and See because it is administered coolly, largely offscreen, at the scale of one family.

rungs.title: Come and See
rungs.why: Anchor. Cruelty at the scale of annihilation, sustained, and put in front of the camera rather than implied.

weakestAdjacency.risk: A scorer reading 'cruelty' as 'how much the characters suffer' could lift Bicycle Thieves above Balthazar, since its ending is the more crushing of the two.

poleCaveat.film: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom
poleCaveat.corpusKey: salo or the 120 days of sodom
poleCaveat.note: Present in the corpus and plausibly ABOVE the high anchor. The cruelty pole is therefore not pinned at 90 by Come and See, and scores above 90 must stay legal.

alternates.corpusKey: salo or the 120 days of sodom
alternates.title: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom
alternates.note: Do NOT use at rank 4 without also moving Come and See; see poleCaveat.

cruelty.corpusNote: The corpus holds only Haneke's 2007 English-language remake, not the 1997 original. It is his own shot-for-shot reconstruction, so the axis position is unchanged, but the ladder must name the film the corpus actually has.

irony.measures: The distance between what the film shows and what it means — whether the film stands behind its own images.
irony.doesNotMeasure: Comedy. Playtime is very funny and almost wholly sincere; a humourless film can be pure irony.

rungs.title: The Tree of Life
rungs.why: It addresses God in whispered voiceover and offers no defence against being laughed at — there is no gap at all between image and intent.

rungs.title: Amarcord
rungs.why: The feeling is unironic memory, but the telling is caricature delivered by a town chronicler nobody is asked to believe, so the film keeps one step back from what it plainly loves.

rungs.title: Barry Lyndon
rungs.why: Above Amarcord because the distance is policy rather than tone: the narrator forecloses each event before it happens and withdraws sympathy on purpose, and that stance never lifts — though the images themselves are meant.

rungs.title: Brazil
rungs.why: Above Barry Lyndon because image, tone and plot are all turned against themselves at once, and the film revokes its own happy ending as a delusion — but its irony is aimed at its world, not at cinema.

rungs.title: Pierrot le Fou
rungs.why: Anchor. The irony reaches the medium itself: characters address the camera about being in a film, speech is quotation, and the form is dismantled while running.

weakestAdjacency.risk: HIGHEST-RISK ADJACENCY IN THIS FILE. Amarcord's grotesquerie is pervasive enough that a scorer may read it as more ironic than Barry Lyndon's cool narration. The argument for the order given is that Amarcord's affection is sincere while its telling is not, whereas Barry Lyndon withholds affection as method.
weakestAdjacency.ownerDecision: If the owner does not accept that distinction, swap rank 2 for the alternate below rather than reordering — an ambivalent rung poisons the gate.

alternates.title: Do the Right Thing
alternates.note: Cleaner rank 2 if Amarcord is judged too ironic: every character is played straight and felt, and the irony is only structural — a film that refuses to endorse its own conclusion.

alternates.title: Network
alternates.note: Alternate rank 4. Rejected as first choice because its central lament is sincere, which makes rank 3 vs 4 closer than it should be.

alternates.title: Dr. Strangelove
alternates.note: Rejected on the no-shared-director rule only: it would put Kubrick at both ranks 3 and 4, letting the scorer satisfy the ladder from the crew graph.

irony.finding: This is the axis where a defensible middle was hardest to find, and the reason is recorded in unavailableCandidates: the natural rank-2 film (The Apartment — sincere romance inside a satirical machine) is not in the corpus.

ambiguity.measures: How much the film refuses to settle — what is still unknowable when it ends.
ambiguity.doesNotMeasure: Complication. A dense plot that fully closes scores low; a simple film that withholds one decisive fact forever scores high.

rungs.title: Goodfellas
rungs.why: Everything is narrated, explained and closed — including the moral, which the voiceover delivers to camera.

rungs.title: Vertigo
rungs.why: The mechanism is confessed outright at the midpoint rather than withheld; what stays open is only motive and the abruptness of the last thirty seconds.

rungs.title: Blowup
rungs.why: Above Vertigo because its central fact is withheld permanently and its evidence literally erased — but the hole is local: the world around it stays entirely legible.

rungs.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
rungs.why: Above Blowup because it explains nothing about its decisive events at all, so the ambiguity is global rather than local — and below Mulholland Drive because the line of the narrative is unbroken and what happened is never in doubt, only what it means.

rungs.title: Mulholland Drive
rungs.why: Anchor. Identity, chronology and reality give way together, so not even the events survive to be interpreted.

weakestAdjacency.risk: A scorer counting unanswered questions rather than weighing them could invert these: Blowup leaves one enormous question, 2001 leaves a smaller number of larger ones.

alternates.title: L'Avventura
alternates.note: Direct substitute for Blowup — same shape of withholding (a disappearance never explained, a plot abandoned mid-film), same director, so swap one for the other and not both in.

alternates.title: Rashomon
alternates.note: Alternate rank 3 if a non-Antonioni middle is wanted; its ambiguity is of testimony rather than of fact.

fracture.measures: How far the telling departs from a single forward order — displacement, permutation, and whether any order can be recovered at all.
fracture.doesNotMeasure: Difficulty. A perfectly linear film can be baffling; a fractured one can be easy to follow.

rungs.title: Tokyo Story
rungs.why: Anchor. One order, one direction, no displacement of any kind — the ellipses between scenes never break the sequence.

rungs.title: Sunset Boulevard
rungs.why: A single frame displaces the whole film — it is narrated from the end by a dead man — but inside that frame the body of the film runs straight through with no further break.

rungs.title: Citizen Kane
rungs.why: Above Sunset Boulevard because the telling is broken into five overlapping accounts told out of order — yet each is dated and attributed, and they reassemble into one uncontested chronology.

rungs.title: Memento
rungs.why: Above Citizen Kane because chronology is systematically inverted and interleaved and is never restored on screen — and below Mulholland Drive because a determinate order does exist and can be recovered exactly.

rungs.title: Mulholland Drive
rungs.why: Anchor. No ordering reconciles the two halves, so unlike every rung below it there is nothing to recover.

weakestAdjacency.risk: Both are fully recoverable, so the distinction is degree of systematic inversion rather than kind. A scorer that treats multiple narrators as the strongest form of fracture could put Kane above Memento.

poleCaveat.note: Present in the corpus and plausibly ABOVE the high anchor — it withholds even whether the events occurred. The fracture pole is not pinned at 90 by Mulholland Drive.

alternates.title: Rashomon
alternates.note: Alternate rank 4 only if Rashomon is NOT used on the ambiguity ladder — no film may sit on two ladders.

unavailableCandidates.title: The Apartment
unavailableCandidates.consequence: Forced the substitution to Amarcord, which is the file's least secure adjacency.

unavailableCandidates.title: Pulp Fiction
unavailableCandidates.consequence: Memento used instead; arguably the better rung anyway, since its inversion is systematic rather than episodic.

unavailableCandidates.title: Umberto D.
unavailableCandidates.consequence: None — Bicycle Thieves covers the same position.
